<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
Let \( S_i, S_j \in \mathcal{U} \) be deterministic systems such that \( \mathcal{F}_{S_i} \not\equiv \mathcal{F}_{S_j} \). Then there exists a transformation \( \Phi \) such that:
\[
\Phi\left(\mathcal{F}_{S_i}(P_{S_i}, t)\right) \neq \Phi\left(\mathcal{F}_{S_j}(P_{S_j}, t)\right)
\]
for all \( t \in \mathbb{T} \), provided \( \mathcal{F}_{S_i} \) and \( \mathcal{F}_{S_j} \) belong to a class of structurally expressive maps (e.g., analytic or piecewise continuous).
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
